definitions.meaning: knocked down flat onto the ground
baffled, left with no idea what to say

explanation.surface: Someone is both brought down and baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knocked to the ground and to be utterly baffled are both senses of being floored, one literal and one figurative.

indicators.note: disposition here means arrangement, so the letters of endearing are disposed afresh

explanation.surface: A drink described as sweet-natured and charming by temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cordial' looks like an adjective, warm and friendly, matching 'endearing'; it is the noun, a syrupy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet pomegranate syrup, a classic fruit cordial mixed into drinks.

parts.note: a shore is a timber prop or support, as used to shore up a wall

explanation.surface: A support stands on solid ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the beach or the land rather than at sea is the meaning of the adverb.

definitions.meaning: a disorder of the blood, read literally

explanation.surface: A blood disorder that also sours relations.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase means diseased blood; idiomatically it means lasting hostility. 'causing' merely links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for long-standing hostility or resentment between parties is the same phrase as a literal blood disorder.

parts.note: French for a thunderbolt or lightning strike, used figuratively for a sudden overwhelming event such as love at first sight

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally a stroke of lightning, means a sudden unexpected shock, which the English idiom also expresses.

clue.text: Kind-hearted actor is an ineffective altruist

definitions.meaning: read literally, one who does good deeds out of kindness
the usual sense: a well-meaning but naive or unrealistic reformer

explanation.surface: A kindly performer turns out to be a well-meaning but useless helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actor' suggests a performer on stage, but it simply means one who acts, a doer.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is used, often disparagingly, for a well-intentioned but impractical philanthropist, yet literally means someone who performs good deeds.

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
ease means rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A trainee is allowed to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To let a property is to rent it out under a contract, a synonym.

clue.text: South American banker leaves gold with old firm

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
in can mean along with, as milk in tea is tea with milk
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A Latin American financier walks out, leaving bullion with an established company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river, something with banks. 'leaves' just links the definition to the wordplay; Orinoco is also a variety of tobacco leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is one of the great rivers of Venezuela and Colombia, and a river is something with banks.

clue.text: Erupts angrily when given bell-bottomed trousers

definitions.meaning: bursts suddenly into rage, like a flame shooting up
trousers that widen from the knee, fashionable in the 1970s

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper on being handed a pair of seventies trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when given' just links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for sudden outbursts of temper and a plural noun for wide-legged seventies trousers share one spelling.

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
a cab is a taxi; the 's simply joins it to what follows
in is used for coming back, as when a taxi is in after its shift

explanation.surface: Logging a taxi's journey back from a stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin built of logs is a simple rustic dwelling out in the countryside, so a modest house in the country.

clue.text: Rumbled because the bell wasn't answered

definitions.meaning: exposed, as a cheat whose deception is discovered
the caller discovered the householder was not at home

explanation.surface: Someone was exposed because nobody came to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'because' links the senses; the second is read literally, as a caller learning the occupant is not in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be discovered in a deception is idiomatic; literally a caller who gets no answer has discovered that you are away.

parts.note: O is a round shape
CE is the Church of England
a lot is a plot of ground

explanation.surface: A wild cat turns up around a churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal around CE, but it simply supplies O, and 'appearing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

parts.note: read as something put on the head (capital, from Latin caput) as a garment one is invested with, not money put into a business

explanation.definitionFit: Hats and helmets are what one wears on the top of one's body, so they clothe that part.

parts.note: opera is the plural of opus, a work

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of rule is wanted

explanation.surface: A factory hand works to rule, as in an industrial go-slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works to rule' reads as an industrial action phrase, but 'works' gives OPERA and 'rule, initially' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a machine is called its operator.

parts.note: read as marine fare of a celestial kind, food from the sea named after a winged messenger of God

explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fish with wing-like fins takes its name from a heavenly being.

clue.text: Don't disregard one of the sappers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps nicknamed the sappers
a member is one of a group

explanation.surface: An instruction not to overlook a particular army engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sappers are military engineers; in the British Army they form the Royal Engineers, RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in mind is the opposite of forgetting or ignoring it.

clue.text: Then read about his devotion to the cause

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of then read are moved around

explanation.surface: Reading on about a man's commitment to his cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: a follower is known by his devotion to the cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a party or belief is characterised by loyalty to it.

clue.text: Order yardmen back to capital gallery

indicators.note: back tells us the word for yardmen runs from right to left

parts.note: the CID, the detectives of Scotland Yard
the Tate is an art gallery in London, the capital

explanation.surface: Instructing yard workers to return to a gallery in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yardmen' suggests labourers, but means Scotland Yard detectives, CID, turned to DIC by 'back'; the Tate is London's art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a command is to lay down what must be done.

definitions.meaning: fresh and stimulating, as sea air

explanation.surface: Holding something up turns out to be refreshing.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting with struts and stimulating like cold air both take this word.

clue.text: Inn and hotels constructed by railway

indicators.note: constructed means the letters of hotels are built into a new form

explanation.surface: An inn and some hotels built beside the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a pub or inn offering lodging.

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa, the dominant (fifth note) is sol
an ace is an expert, a master

explanation.surface: A forceful master figure offers consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dominant' looks like an adjective for a strong person; it is the musical fifth degree of the scale, sol.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolation in grief or distress is a synonym.

clue.text: In Madagascar cereals are in short supply

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words Madagascar cereals

explanation.surface: Cereal crops on Madagascar are running low.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is hard to obtain because there is too little of it.

clue.text: Two bands joined by Richard starkey

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
an O is a round band shape

explanation.surface: A drummer joins two musical groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bands' suggests musical groups, apt for a Beatle, but means circles. Richard Starkey is the real name of Ringo Starr.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles drummer was born with this real name and performed under his stage name.

clue.text: A type to exhibit brazen effrontery

definitions.meaning: to put on a shameless, impudent front

explanation.surface: A certain sort of person who flaunts shameless cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A type' looks like a kind of person; it is a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy printed letters are one sense; showing a brazen countenance is the other.

parts.note: read as one who eats creatures of its own same kind

explanation.definitionFit: One who eats the flesh of its own species devours its own kind.

clue.text: Accountants in love may gamble therein

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Accountants who are infatuated might go and bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaming house is where one plays roulette and cards for money.

clue.text: Last resort for soldiers going to lectures

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, soldiers
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: As a final option, troops are sent to classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Having resort to something is turning to it for help, often when nothing else is left.
